note: Disaster tabletop simulator scenarios (Disaster Preparedness and Response, practice page). Injects are released on the exercise clock (minutes) or by the facilitator. Actions are what a team member says aloud; the recorder taps them. No individual is scored.

scenarios.title: Typhoon: Signal No. 3 by Thursday
scenarios.setting: A 24-station unit. Landfall is forecast for Thursday morning. Thursday's group has 40 patients. Eight staff live where roads flood first.

injects.text: Tuesday 7:00 p.m. PAGASA forecasts Signal No. 3 for your area by Wednesday night.
injects.point: Activate at the trigger, log the time, call staff first (Modules 3 and 5).

injects.text: Only 11 staff can work an added Wednesday evening shift (18 chairs).
actions: Thursday list flagged for the nephrologist
Nephrologist decision on early dialysis requested
Receiving units contacted for the rest
injects.point: Early dialysis is the nephrologist's decision; the unit supplies facts and limits (Module 5).

injects.text: Two nurses cannot come in: their barangay roads are already flooding.
actions: Minimum staffing with an ACLS-current nurse confirmed
Unit van and overnight stay arranged
injects.point: Nobody travels onto flooded roads; set a last safe session time (Module 5).

injects.text: Patient 14 has not answered two calls; his last potassium was 6.4 mmol/L.
actions: Second number and family contact tried
Social worker or barangay health worker asked to help
injects.point: Two numbers and a family contact; escalate a high-risk patient who cannot be reached (Modules 3 and 10).

injects.text: The receiving unit's contact person no longer works there.
actions: Main line called for the current contact
Fix recorded for the after-action report
injects.point: Receiving-unit contacts are checked every year (Module 3).

injects.text: Saturday: the unit can reopen, but the water room was flooded and results are pending.
actions: Unit stays closed until all five gates are signed
Urgent patients placed by the nephrologist
injects.point: Five signed restart gates; a verbal release is not a release (Module 11).

scenarios.title: Earthquake: magnitude 6.8 at 9:40 a.m.
scenarios.setting: A second-floor unit, 16 patients connected, 5 staff. Strong shaking for about 40 seconds.

injects.text: Strong shaking begins. Ceiling panels fall near Station 4.
actions: Staff low beside patients, shielding heads and access arms
injects.point: Patients stay connected and covered; staff stay low beside them (Module 6).

injects.text: The shaking stops. A saline pole has tipped at Station 9.
actions: Machines then room (gas, fire, cracks, exits) checked
injects.point: Patients first, then machines, then the room, then a count (Module 6).

injects.text: The patient at Station 12 is pulling at his lines, demanding to be taken off.
actions: Access arm held and needles checked
Patient told staff will take him off if the unit leaves
injects.point: Calm, specific words prevent self-disconnection (Modules 4 and 6).

injects.text: Aftershock.
injects.point: The same rule for every shaking (Module 6).

injects.text: The facilities officer reports a new crack across a column. Foam is seen in the venous line at Station 4.
actions: Evacuation ordered by the incident lead
Emergency take-off by staff with the blood rule
Catheter clamps closed before separating lines
injects.point: Visible structural damage means evacuate; never return blood that may contain air (Modules 6 and 7).

injects.text: At the assembly point, one staff member is missing from the count.
actions: Census nurse reports to the incident lead
Rescuers told where the person was last seen
injects.point: Account for everyone; nobody re-enters a damaged building (Module 7).

scenarios.title: Fire: smoke from the reprocessing room
scenarios.setting: A ground-floor unit, 12 patients connected: three use wheelchairs, one came on a stretcher.

injects.text: 2:10 p.m. Smoke is coming from under the reprocessing room door. No alarm yet.
actions: BFP called by someone without a patient
injects.point: RACE: rescue, alarm, contain, extinguish or evacuate, done by different people (Module 7).

injects.text: A nurse with a connected patient wants to fetch the extinguisher.
injects.point: Never leave a connected patient to fetch an extinguisher (Module 7).

injects.text: The fire is growing; smoke reaches the corridor.
actions: Oxygen not in use turned off
Take-off by staff: clamp and disconnect
injects.point: In a fire, clamp and disconnect is usually right (Module 7).

injects.text: The stretcher patient's helper is on break.
actions: Backup helper assigned from the evacuation sheet
Patients nearest the smoke moved first
injects.point: Mobility categories and helpers are set at the start of the shift (Module 7).

injects.text: At the assembly point, one patient is not checked off.
actions: Firefighters told where she was last seen
injects.point: A named census nurse; firefighters search (Module 7).

scenarios.title: Long power outage: brownout at 4:20 p.m.
scenarios.setting: A 15-station unit, 12 patients connected. The utility failed at 4:20 p.m.; the generator started.

injects.text: 4:20 p.m. Utility power fails. The generator starts.
actions: Power status and fuel runtime asked of the technician
injects.point: Patients first; ask for the runtime at the start (Module 8).

injects.text: 5:10 p.m. The fuel delivery has not come. The generator is at 30% fuel and will run out within the hour.
injects.point: A known end time allows a normal take-off with working alarms (Module 8).

injects.text: 6:05 p.m. The generator stops. Two patients are still connected; machines on battery.
actions: Walk the floor; uncover needle sites
injects.point: The first ten minutes: patients first, then decide (Module 8).

injects.text: Batteries run down; blood pumps stop.
actions: Eyes on the venous line until the clamp is closed
injects.point: Without power, the operator's eyes replace the air detector (Module 8).

injects.text: At one station the circuit is clotting.
actions: Clamp and cut; not forced back
injects.point: Never force a clotted circuit back (Module 8).

injects.text: The utility is back. The water system restarts.
actions: No new starts until water checks are done
injects.point: Restart is checked, not assumed (Modules 8 and 11).

scenarios.title: Ashfall after an eruption
scenarios.setting: A 12-station unit. Fine ash covers roads and cars at dawn; PHIVOLCS has raised the volcano alert level.

injects.text: 5:30 a.m. Ash everywhere. The waiting-area windows are open; the rooftop tank cover is loose.
actions: Air intakes covered and tank secured
injects.point: Close, cover, clean (Module 9).

injects.text: Two staff call: roads are slippery and visibility is poor.
injects.point: Staff travel only when safe (Modules 3 and 9).

injects.text: 6:20 a.m. Pre-filter pressure drop rising fast.
injects.point: Ash in the water is a water event; never bypass a filter (Modules 8 and 9).

injects.text: An older patient with lung disease arrives coughing.
injects.point: Examine before connecting (Module 9).

injects.text: The LDRRMO advises evacuation of nearby barangays; six of your patients live there.
injects.point: Find every patient within 24 hours (Module 10).
